clues: The Ripple went out later in the morning than the Tern.
Pearl's lesson came before the Tern's.
Emil sailed later than whoever took the Bluebell.
Walt's lesson was at either 9 a.m. or 11 a.m.
Neither Emil nor Pearl sailed the Bluebell.
The Bluebell went out at either 10 a.m. or noon.
hints: Look at the 9 a.m. row in the bottom box, where times meet boats. Which boats could possibly have gone out first?
Comparisons rule out the ends. Which boats do clues 1 and 2 keep off 9 a.m.? Then see what clue 6 says.
So the Whelk went out at 9 a.m. Then clue 3 keeps the Bluebell off noon, so by clue 6 it went out at 10 a.m.

solution.key_idea: Clues 1, 2 and 6 leave 9 a.m. to the Whelk, and clue 3 then pins the Bluebell to 10 a.m.
steps: Clue 1 keeps the Ripple off 9 a.m., clue 2 the Tern, and clue 6 the Bluebell. So the Whelk went out at 9 a.m.
By clue 3, Emil sailed after the Bluebell, so the Bluebell was not out at noon. By clue 6, it went out at 10 a.m.
Clue 1 keeps the Tern off noon, so the Tern went out at 11 a.m. and the Ripple at noon.
Neither Emil nor Pearl sailed the Bluebell (clue 5), and Walt's lesson was not at 10 a.m. (clue 4). So Carmen sailed the Bluebell.
By clue 2, Pearl sailed before the 11 a.m. Tern, and 10 a.m. was Carmen's. So Pearl took the Whelk at 9 a.m.
By clue 4, Walt sailed the Tern at 11 a.m., which leaves Emil the Ripple at noon.
solution.epilogue: Felix wrote the certificates at last. Pearl had the Whelk at 9 a.m., Carmen the Bluebell at 10, Walt the Tern at 11, and Emil the Ripple at noon.

tip: Turn the question around: ask not "When did the Ripple sail?" but "Which boat could go first?"
story: Felix gave four sailing lessons on Saturday morning, one each hour, each in a different little boat from his yard. He kept the lesson sheet in his head, which he calls shipshape. It is mostly shipshape. Every student is owed a certificate naming the boat and the hour, so who sailed when, and in which boat?
